items.stem: At which point does threat modeling add the most value in the SDLC?

options.text: During design, before code is written
options.rationale: Correct: modeling threats in design lets teams remove flaws cheaply before they are built in.
Post-deployment is the most expensive place to discover design flaws.
Marketing review is unrelated to technical threat modeling.

options.text: Never; scanning tools make it unnecessary
options.rationale: Scanners catch implementation bugs, not design-level threats.

items.explanation: Correct: modeling threats in design lets teams remove flaws cheaply before they are built in.

items.stem: Which tool type analyses your third-party and open-source dependencies for known vulnerabilities?

options.rationale: Correct: SCA inventories dependencies and flags components with known vulnerabilities.
SAST analyses your own source code, not dependency inventories.
DAST tests a running application from the outside.
A style linter does not track dependency vulnerabilities.

items.explanation: Correct: SCA inventories dependencies and flags components with known vulnerabilities.

items.stem: Which TWO practices reflect shifting security left? (Select TWO)

options.text: Writing testable security requirements during requirements gathering
options.rationale: Correct: defining security needs early makes them part of the build, not an afterthought.

options.text: Running SAST automatically on pull requests
options.rationale: Correct: catching code flaws at PR time is earlier and cheaper than post-release.

options.text: Performing all security testing only after go-live
options.rationale: Testing only after go-live is the opposite of shifting left.

options.text: Delegating security entirely to an external audit at year end
options.rationale: An annual external audit alone leaves flaws in place for most of the cycle.

items.explanation: Correct: defining security needs early makes them part of the build, not an afterthought.
